Query Dremio as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__dremio.R
oauth_db_dremio.Rd

Open a Flight SQL connection with the visitor's current OAuth access token. The connection uses adbi and Apache Arrow's ADBC Flight SQL driver, and supports DBI queries and Arrow results.

Usage

oauth_db_dremio(
  authorization,
  host,
  ...,
  port = 32010L,
  driver = "flightsql",
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  timeout = 30,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

host

One Flight SQL endpoint hostname or IPv4 address, without a protocol or port. Use a Dremio endpoint configured for TLS and bearer authentication.

...

Result option bigint, passed to adbi's DBI::dbConnect() method. Other native options cannot be supplied.

port

Flight SQL port, default 32010 for self-hosted Dremio.

driver

Installed ADBC driver name, manifest path or shared-library path. The default "flightsql" selects the driver installed with dbc install flightsql.

ca_bundle

Optional path to a PEM file containing trusted CA certificates. NULL uses the driver's system trust roots.

timeout

Positive timeout in seconds for each Flight SQL connection, query, fetch or update RPC. This is not a deadline for an entire query.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, usually named con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression, then use the connection with DBI. Before sign-in, it waits quietly.

Details

Install adbi, adbcdrivermanager 0.25.0 or later, and the ADBC Flight SQL shared-library driver. The R packages alone do not install that driver. Configure Dremio Enterprise to accept the provider's external JWT access tokens and map their identities to Dremio users. An already acquired Dremio OAuth access token can also be supplied through shinyOAuth.

The helper sends the access token directly as a bearer credential. It does not exchange external JWTs for Dremio tokens or run the driver's OAuth flow. A browser login alone does not configure database access. Dremio Cloud editions and endpoints require separate compatibility checks; see vignette("dremio", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

TLS and certificate verification are required. Credentials, native OAuth settings, headers, URI and TLS settings cannot be overridden in ....

Create the helper inside server() and call con() before each operation. A changed access token replaces the connection on its next use, without replaying completed reactive queries. Account changes, permission loss, sign-out and session end close the connection and outstanding results. The driver holds a fixed bearer during each DBI operation; renewing the Shiny token does not update an ongoing query or fetch. A failed query is not replayed. Reopening loses SQL session state; a submitted query may continue after the local connection closes.

See also

vignette("dremio", package = "shinyOAuthDB") for driver installation, provider settings and a complete Shiny app.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_dremio(auth$connection, host = "dremio.example.org")
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT CURRENT_USER AS database_user")
})
} # }
